newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-HARVEY, LEHMANN PARTNERSHIP SCUPPERS WINDIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-HARVEY, LEHMANN PARTNERSHIP SCUPPERS WINDIES.

text.p: An unbeaten stand of 132 between Ian Harvey and Darren Lehmann extended West Indies' miserable run as they crashed to a six-wicket defeat against Australia A on Friday.

Harvey hit a straight six off Kenneth Benjamin to take Australia A to 218 for four wickets with more than five overs to spare in response to West Indies' 217 for eight from 50 overs at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.
Harvey finished with 67 and Lehmann 63 to consign West Indies to their seventh successive defeat on tour.
The match had been evenly-poised as Australia A struggled to 86 for four.

Harvey and Lehmann came together after the dismissal of Australia A captain Steve Waugh, caught behind by Junior Murray off Kenneth Benjamin for 12, and savaged the West Indies attack in the absence of pace bowler Courtney Walsh.
Opener Michael Slater, dropped by national selectors before the first test against West Indies last month, hit an aggressive 40 before he was caught by Adrian Griffith off Nixon McLean.
Matthew Hayden, a rival with Slater for an Australian opening spot, did not help his cause when he was run out for 14 in a clumsy mix-up with his partner.
Both players are vying for the vacancy in the test side caused by injury to Matthew Elliott.

The match was also a fitness test for Waugh who missed the second test due to a groin injury. He has been recalled to the Australian one-day side for Sunday's World Series match against Pakistan in Adelaide.
Shivnarine Chanderpaul was the stalwart of the West Indies' innings, hitting 72 as star batsman Brian Lara again failed to make a big score.
Lara, acting as captain in Walsh's absence, hit several good shots before being bowled for 33 by spinner Geoff Foley.
Foley and pace bowler Michael Kasprowicz took two wickets each in West Indies' innings.
West Indies suffered heavy defeats in the first two tests against Australia and are without a win after two matches against the same opponents in the triangular World Series tournament.
